newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand and bonds ended a see-saw day in bullish mood on Friday with dealers looking for further gains in both markets next week.

The currency was knocked lower initially by a big importer order but was salvaged by heavy dollar sales out of London and a flood of exporter orders which took the rand to its best levels against the dollar since early December.
"We had a large seller of dollars out of the U.K. and there were obviously a few guys who were caught long above the 4.65 level who started baling out as well," said one forex trader.
"I reckon if we can stay below 4.65 we could possibly go close to 4.60 next week," he added.
Bond traders said some of the offshore dollars sold for rand were invested in the local debt market, sweeping yields lower after a rocky start.

Underpinning the current upbeat mood was an emerging consensus that the rand would stabilise in 1997, falling a modest 6-7 percent in line with inflation differentials, after its 29 percent tumble against the greenback in 1996.
"I think we are in for a different ball game this year on the rand," said Peter Lane, head of treasury at UAL Merchant Bank.
"The rand is going to trade in a much tighter band this year. It will depreciate, but at a controlled rate broadly in line with inflation differentials."
Other traders said that new-found stability -- if maintained -- would encourage overseas investors back into South African bonds for yield play and could see the market move firmer again next week.
"It looks like 15.45 percent (on the R150) is the next major resistance," said a dealer with one of the "big four" banks.

The market mood was also being helped by signs of fiscal rectitude on the part of the government, with latest figures for showing government revenue up a healthy 17 percent in the first nine months of the year.
"The latest figures show revenues are doing very well, although income tax is enjoying a boost from economic growth which is now in the past," said Dawie Roodt, economist at brokers Equisec.
The market once again shrugged off a disappointing daily money market shortage, which remained stubbornly above 10 billion rand at 10.444 billion rand on Thursday from 10.131 billion on Wednesday.
Leading banks quoted their three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.25-17.50 percent while 90-day BA rates were also unchanged at 16.60-16.85 percent.
At the long end of the curve, the R150 was yielding 15.57 after morning peak of 15.685 and afternoon low of 15.53 versus 15.62 percent late on Thursday.
The rand finished at 4.6425/6475 after briefly touching 4.6300/6350 from 4.6555/6605 at 1400 GMT on Thursday.
Against the crosses it was trading at 7.7757/7887 on sterling from 7.8041/8171 while on the mark it was at 0.3458/3463 from 0.3420/3425.
Foreigners sold a net 68.35 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 268.44 million rands on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 36.42 million rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 8.68 billion rand.
-- Ben Hirschler, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
